name: Nashville
character: Nashville's older neighborhoods, from East Nashville to Inglewood and Sylvan Park, are full of mature oaks, maples, and hackberries planted decades before the streets around them got busy.
angle: Big legacy trees next to closer-together lots and older utility lines mean more careful, close-quarters work than a wide-open suburban yard.

name: Portland
character: Portland still carries its farming roots, with strawberry fields on the edge of town giving way to in-town lots shaded by tall, older trees.
angle: A lot of properties here back up to open farmland or fence lines, so windbreak trees and field-edge growth end up on the job list along with the yard.

name: White House
character: White House has grown fast along US-31W, with new subdivisions built right up against what used to be pasture and woodland.
angle: Newer construction here often leaves builder-grade trees planted too close to the house, plus tree lines along the property edge that never got thinned.

name: Springfield
character: Springfield is the Robertson County seat, with a historic courthouse square and older residential streets lined with big, established shade trees.
angle: Those older shade trees are usually healthy, but decades of growth means storm-damaged limbs and overdue crown work are common calls.

name: Mount Juliet
character: Mount Juliet is one of the fastest-growing cities in Middle Tennessee, with new subdivisions going in around Providence Marketplace and older farmland still holding out on the edges of town.
angle: New-build yards usually need young trees shaped up early, while the older properties nearby still have big legacy trees that need real attention.

name: Lebanon
character: Lebanon's historic square and Cumberland University sit at the center of a city that's grown well past its old town limits along I-40.
angle: Between the older in-town streets and the newer growth toward the interstate, we see everything from mature hardwoods to first-year saplings that need training.

name: Murfreesboro
character: Murfreesboro is the largest city in Middle Tennessee outside Nashville itself, with historic districts near MTSU and subdivisions spreading out in every direction.
angle: That mix means jobs range from tight, tree-lined in-town lots to newer subdivisions where storm damage and stump removal are the more common calls.

name: Franklin
character: Franklin's historic downtown and surrounding neighborhoods are known for heavy tree canopy, with big hardwoods that predate a lot of the houses around them.
angle: Property owners here tend to want trees preserved and shaped carefully, not just cut back, especially near the historic district.

name: Brentwood
character: Brentwood's rolling, wooded lots and larger properties mean a lot of mature tree cover packed into HOA-governed subdivisions.
angle: Bigger lots and taller trees closer to the house make careful, well-equipped removal and trimming the norm rather than the exception.

name: Madison
character: Madison's post-war neighborhoods were built with big front and back yards, and the shade trees planted back then have had 60-plus years to grow into them.
angle: A lot of the calls we get here are legacy trees that have outgrown the yard, with roots and limbs now pushing into driveways, fences, and roof lines.

name: Hermitage
character: Hermitage takes its name from Andrew Jackson's historic estate nearby, and the community around Percy Priest Lake mixes older wooded lots with newer development.
angle: Lake-adjacent properties and older wooded lots both mean bigger trees, so storm cleanup and full removals come up more than routine trims.

name: Gallatin
character: Gallatin is the Sumner County seat, sitting on Old Hickory Lake with a historic downtown square and neighborhoods that stretch from lakefront to farmland.
angle: Lakefront trees take a beating from wind off the water, so storm damage and leaning trees near the shoreline are a regular part of the work here.

name: Hendersonville
character: Hendersonville is one of the larger Nashville-area suburbs, stretched along Old Hickory Lake with a mix of lakefront homes and inland residential streets.
angle: Between lake winds and dense residential lots, we handle a steady mix of storm cleanup, tree removal, and stump grinding for yards that are ready to be usable again.
